scope: Repository implementation status for the bounded synthetic F7-LAS reference workflow; this is not an assessment of any production deployment.

controls.title: Prompt Version Control
controls.limitations: Prompt files are versioned in Git, but the repository is not a production prompt store and branch protection is a separate repository setting.

controls.title: Role & Scope Definition
controls.limitations: Structured role and scope placeholders exist, while the canonical workflow admits only one fixed synthetic actor and scope.

controls.title: Prohibited Actions
controls.limitations: Prompt prohibitions are present as soft-policy templates; hard enforcement is demonstrated only for the fixed canonical action.

controls.title: Abstain & Escalate Behavior
controls.limitations: Escalation rules are represented in prompt templates, but no interactive agent or human escalation service is implemented.

controls.title: Prompt Change Control
controls.limitations: CI validates prompt structure, but production approval records and enforced repository protection remain outside the codebase.

controls.title: Prompt Security Testing
controls.limitations: The repository has structural prompt validation but no periodic prompt-injection or jailbreak test program and findings workflow.

controls.title: RAG Source Inventory
controls.limitations: An illustrative source allowlist exists without owners, classifications, lifecycle governance, or a deployed retrieval inventory.

controls.title: Access-Controlled RAG Gateway
controls.limitations: No authenticated retrieval gateway, rate limiting, deployed source authorization, or retrieval-call logging is provided.

controls.title: Curation & Retirement Process
controls.limitations: No operational content-owner approval, scheduled review, update, or retirement workflow is implemented.

controls.title: Poisoning Defenses
controls.limitations: No deployed ingestion pipeline, restricted authorship mechanism, poisoning detector, or high-impact content review is implemented.

controls.title: Treat Retrieved Content as Untrusted
controls.limitations: The canonical path records fixed synthetic evidence and never executes retrieved text, but it does not implement a live RAG pipeline.

controls.title: RAG Injection Testing
controls.limitations: There is no adversarial retrieval index or automated retrieved-content injection evaluation in the supported workflow.

controls.title: Planner Identification
controls.limitations: The canonical deterministic planner is explicitly identified, but the illustrative planners are not a deployed orchestration architecture.

controls.title: Planning Contracts
controls.limitations: The canonical plan has fixed action, step, and duration limits, but it is not a general per-agent contract with a configurable allowed-tool set.

controls.title: Bounded Reason–Act Loops
controls.limitations: The canonical path is structurally fixed to one step and one action; it does not implement a reusable loop counter, recursion limit, or runtime wall-clock controller.

controls.title: Explicit Stop Conditions
controls.limitations: Permit, denial, refusal, failure, and recovery outcomes are tested, but no general planner state machine records all catalog stop conditions.

controls.title: Delegation Rules for Multi-Agent
controls.limitations: The supported canonical workflow uses one fixed synthetic actor and contains no multi-agent delegation runtime or enforced call graph.

controls.title: Planner Telemetry
controls.limitations: Plan and audit records preserve the deterministic planner output, but there is no production telemetry sink, dashboard, or retention control.

controls.title: Goal/Role Drift Testing
controls.limitations: The behavioral matrix covers fixed admission and authorization failures but does not provide a goal- or role-drift evaluation suite.

controls.title: Tool Catalog
controls.limitations: A validated illustrative allowlist records owners and risk tiers, while the canonical runtime registers only one fixed synthetic tool.

controls.title: Tool Risk Tiering
controls.limitations: Risk tiers are present in the illustrative allowlist and canonical action, but no general runtime routes all tools according to tier.

controls.title: Read/Write Separation
controls.limitations: The only canonical operation is a synthetic read, but distinct read and write identities or execution environments are not implemented.

controls.title: Least-Privilege Tool Permissions
controls.limitations: The offline synthetic executor has no external credential or IAM role, so real least-privilege permissions are not provisioned or reviewed.

controls.title: Agent-to-Tool Access Control
controls.limitations: The canonical policy binds one actor to one exact tool action, but there is no configurable multi-agent tool entitlement service.

controls.title: Tool Argument Validation
controls.limitations: Implemented for the single canonical synthetic action only; it is not a generic validation service for illustrative tools.

controls.title: Tool Call Telemetry
controls.limitations: Canonical proposed-action, result, and audit records are correlated, but no deployed telemetry pipeline or sanitization service exists.

controls.title: HITL for Tier-3 Tools
controls.limitations: The allowlist represents a high-risk tool requiring HITL and the canonical path enforces synthetic approval, but no Tier-3 tool or live human workflow executes.

controls.title: External PDP/PEP Architecture
controls.limitations: Implemented for one offline OPA decision and in-process PEP path; no network PDP service or production tool gateway is claimed.

controls.title: Policy-as-Code
controls.limitations: Implemented for the canonical Rego and reviewed policy metadata; other policy-engine examples remain illustrative.

controls.title: Decision Outcomes
controls.limitations: The canonical PDP emits permit or deny with obligations; clarify and human referral are architecture outcomes rather than executable PDP results.

controls.title: Tiered Policy Enforcement
controls.limitations: One fixed action always passes through OPA, but general Tier-2 and Tier-3 routing and differentiated obligations are not implemented.

controls.title: Policy Change Management
controls.limitations: CI validates policy changes, while production deployment approval and enforced branch review are repository-administration responsibilities.

controls.title: PDP/PEP Telemetry
controls.limitations: Policy decisions and execution results are correlated in local evidence, but no centralized production audit or incident-response ingestion exists.

controls.title: Segmented Runtime Environment
controls.limitations: Layer 6 is a synthetic in-process executor and provides no separate tenant, account, VM, container, or production segmentation boundary.

controls.title: Network Egress Controls
controls.limitations: The canonical action makes no network call, but no firewall, VNET, VPC, proxy, or enforced egress allowlist is deployed.

evidence.locator: does not enforce a network-isolation boundary

controls.title: Environment Separation (Read vs Remediate)
controls.limitations: Only a read-only synthetic action exists; there is no separate write-capable remediation environment or identity boundary.

controls.title: Identity Per Agent / Sandbox
controls.limitations: Synthetic subject identifiers are evidence fields, not provisioned identities, credentials, or sandbox-specific roles.

controls.title: Sandbox Profile Definitions
controls.limitations: A profile configuration and deterministic profile digest exist, but OS, resource, filesystem, and network restrictions are not enforced by the in-process executor.

controls.title: Ephemeral Sandboxes
controls.limitations: No sandbox is created or destroyed; execution occurs in the current Python process using synthetic data.

controls.title: Blast Radius Statement
controls.limitations: The canonical boundary documents no network or external side effects, but there is no deployment-specific risk acceptance or owner sign-off.

controls.title: Unified Telemetry Schema
controls.limitations: Eight canonical record schemas correlate the supported workflow, but they do not cover every production event type listed by the catalog.

controls.title: Central Telemetry Ingestion
controls.limitations: Evidence is written to a local JSON file and is not sent to a SIEM, XDR, log pipeline, or centralized monitoring service.

controls.title: Detection Rules for Agent Misuse
controls.limitations: No deployable misuse detections, alert rules, correlated incident logic, or alert-history evidence is included.

controls.title: Golden Dataset Evaluation
controls.limitations: CI enforces structural golden thresholds, but the runner does not execute the scenarios against the canonical workflow or score behavioral outcomes.

controls.title: Red-Team & Adversarial Testing
controls.limitations: Negative behavioral tests cover authorization and tampering paths, but there is no periodic prompt, RAG, tool, or sandbox red-team exercise.

controls.title: SLOs for Agent Safety
controls.limitations: Draft SLO examples exist without measured service telemetry, owners, alert thresholds, review records, or an operating service.

controls.title: SBOM Generation
controls.limitations: CI generates a CycloneDX inventory for the locked Python graph; it does not inventory the full runner or establish signed provenance.

controls.title: Dependency Vulnerability Scanning
controls.limitations: The locked Python graph is audited for published vulnerabilities; runner OS and non-Python components are outside this scan.

evidence.locator: Audit dependencies and generate CycloneDX SBOM

controls.title: Framework Version Pinning
controls.limitations: Python dependencies, Actions, OPA, and Gitleaks are pinned for CI; this does not attest the hosted runner image.

controls.title: Plugin & Tool Framework Governance
controls.limitations: The illustrative tool allowlist contains owners and review metadata, but no production plugin admission workflow or enforced approval record exists.

controls.title: Framework Telemetry & Attestation
controls.limitations: CI associates an SBOM artifact with an exact commit SHA, but runtime telemetry lacks framework version and signed build-attestation identifiers.
